events.text: U.S. forces struck Venezuela and captured President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores.
The United States formally withdrew from the World Health Organization.
A winter storm across more than 30 states killed at least 85 people over four days.
A lapse in funding shut down parts of the federal government; it ended Feb. 3.
A second partial shutdown began, centered on Homeland Security funding.
The Supreme Court ruled the President exceeded his authority in imposing tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.
The U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei; Iran retaliated against bases across the Gulf.
A U.S. submarine sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena in the Indian Ocean.
Mojtaba Khamenei was named Iran's new Supreme Leader.
A strike on a girls' elementary school in Minab, Iran, killed 168–180 people; a preliminary U.S. military review found the U.S. responsible.
Israel began a ground invasion of southern Lebanon.
NASA's Artemis II carried four astronauts around the Moon, the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since 1972; it returned April 10.
Hungary's Viktor Orbán lost power after 16 years as Péter Magyar's Tisza Party won the election.
After a ceasefire collapsed and talks in Islamabad failed, the U.S. began a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
The United Arab Emirates left OPEC after about six decades of membership.
The Supreme Court ruled patients can keep accessing the abortion pill mifepristone (Danco Laboratories v. Louisiana).
The President signed the Secure America Act, providing $70 billion for immigration enforcement.
The U.S. and Iran signed the Islamabad Memorandum, lifting both sides' blockades; they agreed on June 28 to stop attacks.
In end-of-term rulings, the Supreme Court upheld state transgender sports bans, affirmed birthright citizenship and struck down campaign finance limits.
The U.S.-Iran ceasefire collapsed after Iran attacked commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.
The U.S. announced 20% fees on Strait of Hormuz cargo and restarted its blockade of Iranian ports.
Spain beat Argentina 1-0 to win the FIFA World Cup, hosted by the U.S., Canada and Mexico.
The U.S. announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods; they took effect on $28 billion of goods Aug. 22.
The Syrian Democratic Forces merged into the Syrian Army.
King Harald V of Norway died; his son became King Haakon VIII.
Congress passed a stopgap bill funding the government through Dec. 11, avoiding an Oct. 1 shutdown.
The Senate rejected, 49-50, a resolution directing U.S. forces out of hostilities with Iran.
The Supreme Court ruled 7-2 the administration can use its expanded SAVE database to help states check voters' citizenship.
After a Trump-Xi summit in Washington, the U.S. and China extended their trade truce to Jan. 10, 2027 and agreed to $60 billion in tariff cuts.
The Supreme Court let the administration resume deportations to third countries while it hears the case in December.
The Transportation Department cut fuel economy standards to 34.9 mpg by model year 2031, down from about 50 mpg.
The United States ended its anti-ISIS military mission in Iraq, withdrawing the last U.S. troops after more than two decades.
